scope: Bounded preventive native-clock renewal in the common SteamVR director. Retain the same FIFO source packet and physical handoff cadence; request one fresh native window if a still-current prediction does not cover the next physical refresh. Applies to D11/D12 and Luke Ross with AFW on or off.
headset_validation: V593 owner reports markedly improved delivery but residual short drops while produced frames remain stable. Actual SteamVR paired 37.5+37.5 trials: V593 shows 877/901 with 4096px images, bounded candidate 898/901. Final production-source repeat shows 900/901. No steady 90 or zero-loss claim; new Valhalla/Luke game validation pending.

hardware_comparison.method: Actual SteamVR/OpenXR D3D12 session on the 90 Hz display. Paired 37.5 Hz inputs produce 75 content submissions/s. Compare identical phase, source rate, image size and environment. Match the second-Submit CPU timestamp uniquely inside native End entry/return with 30 us clock alignment tolerance. All source submissions are matched; exclude only unrelated initialization receipts, never the first source frame.
hardware_comparison.final_probe: Compiled from the exact V594 production runtime, including stage 25. All 901 source submissions matched; 900 shown, one unshown. The preventive guard exercised on 174 packets, at most once per packet.
hardware_comparison.limitations: Sequential controlled trials, not owner game acceptance or proof of universal loss-free output. Earlier bounded trials showed 898/901 at both image sizes; the final-source repeat showed 900/901. Isolated genuine losses remain.

owner_evidence: V593 Valhalla PID35540. Full-run external receipts confirm residual clusters: Djules receives74/shows65 in the worst one-second interval; Reference75/66; Fidelity78/70. Detailed F9 data covers only the final1.983seconds, not the full loss clusters. Stable produced counts do not imply content was shown.
implementation: After preparation and physical deadline selection, preserve V593 expired-cycle recovery. If raw converted native prediction is future but no later than the next physical period after the planned handoff, request one preventive renewal through the existing Wait worker and serialized Begin consumer. A current replacement that remains short is accepted; no unbounded future-horizon loop. Without a valid physical clock, only the prior expired-cycle behavior applies. Recompute the same absolute handoff after native work.

negative_control.assertion: a physical handoff needs one preventive attempt when the native window is short
